pr_title: Insert ESM exports for CommonJS entries
pr_body:
# ↪️ Pull Request

Closes #3586 :

> ```html
> <script type="module" src="./index.js"></script>
> ```
> ```js
> // index.js
> import("./commonjs.js").then(v => console.log(v));
> ```
> ```js
> // commonjs.js
> module.exports = 2;
> ```
> 
> Output:
> `./commonjs.e4b0f555.js` is empty
> without `treeShake`, the output is
> ```js
> // ...
> var $dfc1ea661454a5b57fd7e754dd151b32$exports = {};
> $dfc1ea661454a5b57fd7e754dd151b32$exports = 2;
> ```

This essentially exports `module.exports` as the `default` export in commonjs bundles with `outputFormat: "esmodule"`

issue_context.title: Dynamically importing CommonJS produces empty bundle
comments:
I guess we should, for now, throw an error if the entry asset of the dynamic bundle has CommonJS exports?

The real solution (other than converting CommonJS to esm):
1. if the entry asset of the async bundle has CommonJS exports, do a `global` build (and use the `import()` polyfill), otherwise `esmodule`

For this to work, we need to modify `asset.env.outputFormat` after the `hoist` step (is this possible already?)

2. a "split" could happen is if a bundlegroup gets split into multiple bundles and if the module that is being imported is a CommonJS module, we need to generate a matching export

This situation is currently hard to test, as it would only happen when the bundler detects that the bundle is getting too large. We might need a bundler that does this controllably

example:
```js
import ReactDOM from "react-dom"; // is a CommonJS module, the bundler wants to turn this into a seperate bundle
ReactDOM.render();
``` 
would generate bundles equivalent to these:
```js
import ReactDOM from "react-dom"; // this is "unrolled" after scope hoisting
export default ReactDOM; // this will become `export default $123acd$var$...`
```
and
```js
import ReactDOM from "./the_other_bundle.js";
ReactDOM.render();
```

3. a user-set `outputFormat: esmodule` on an asset with CommonJS should throw, we don't know which exports should be exposed (this is what `rollup-plugin-commonjs` tries as well and requires hand-tuning)

@devongovett ?
`import()` returns the entire module namespace. Should we just map the common JS `module.exports` object to that namespace if we detect it is CommonJS?
